children: UNICEF and Geneva-based global vaccine group Gavi said on Thursday that they have reached an agreement to cut the price of the Mosquirix malaria vaccine by about 40%.

The deal, executed by UNICEF and financially backed by Gavi, is expected to generate around $50 million in savings between 2027 and 2029 and will bring the price of the vaccine down to €5.50 ($6.16) per dose
The vaccine, called Mosquirix or RTS,S/AS01, developed by GSK
and the non-profit PATH and is now being transferred from GSK to Bharat Biotech for future supply

GSK is working on a technology transfer to Bharat Biotech, and will continue to supply the adjuvant part of the vaccine to Bharat when the Indian drugmaker fully takes over production of the shot by 2028
The lower price is expected to take effect by early 2027, and it builds on the transfer of the vaccine’s production to a developing-country manufacturer, Gavi and UNICEF said
The agreement is subject to regulatory and manufacturing milestones, which must be met before UNICEF begins procuring doses, including WHO prequalification of a new manufacturing facility

"This new agreement follows major investment by both GSK and Bharat Biotech to help secure long-term equitable access to RTS,S/AS01 for many more children," GSK's chief global health officer, Harmony P. Garges said
GSK and Bharat Biotech also said last year they plan to cut the price of the Mosquirix vaccine below $5 per dose by 2028
Gavi and UNICEF also struck a deal last year to cut the price of another malaria vaccine made by the Serum Institute of India by 25%
